subject: elephant
pitch: A gentle African elephant calf. Wrinkly slate-grey skin with a dusty, reddish tint from rolling in the dirt, huge fan-shaped ears with a pink flush on the inside, a curious trunk curling forward, stubby baby tusks, long lashes over kind brown eyes, a little tufted tail and round, padded feet with pale toenails.
reasoning:
I'm planning the elephant calf's proportions and scale, aiming for a stylized but characterful build around 1.1m shoulder height, and sketching out the main body parts I'll construct from primitives like spheres and cylinders.

I'm now working out the head dome, tapered leg cylinders with flattened feet and toenail details, and the fan-shaped ears using extruded shapes with a pink inner layer, positioning them to flap outward from the sides of the head.

For the trunk, I'm chaining a series of overlapping spheres with gradually decreasing radius along a curved path to fake a tapered, slightly wrinkled tube, curling it forward, down, then up at the tip. I'm also placing stubby cream-colored tusk cones near the mouth and dark brown eye spheres on the sides of the head.

Now I'm detailing the eyes with iris and pupil spheres plus thin dark lash boxes, adding a thin hanging tail with a dark tuft cluster, and generating a canvas-based wrinkle texture (used as map/bumpMap) with a dusty reddish overlay for the skin, alongside color choices for ears, tusks, nails, eyes, lashes, and tail tuft. I'm also sizing the legs and feet proportionally under the body.

Now I'm working through the geometry math to position legs, feet, toenails, and the head relative to the ellipsoid body, calculating surface offsets so the head and eyes sit correctly on the body's curvature, placing eyes at roughly (±0.26, 1.06, 0.66) based on the head sphere's surface geometry.

Defining the eyelashes as small rotated boxes arranged along the upper eye arc, and sketching the ear shape as a curved fan using quadratic bezier paths positioned on the sides of the head.

I'm figuring out the extrusion and rotation for the ears so they sit flat against the sides of the head, with the shape's plane facing outward and slightly back, positioning the left ear at the appropriate offset.

For the inner pink detail, I need it positioned so it's visible from the front where the ear flares outward, which means placing it on the inner-facing side slightly offset from the main ear shape, scaled down a bit smaller than the outer ear.

For skin, I'm setting up a canvas texture with a base fill color and adding some randomized wrinkle curves for texture.

For the trunk, I'm plotting a curve of points from root to tip, sampling spheres of tapering radius along that path to build an overlapping segmented shape, with the tip curling upward. I'll skip the nostril detail and consider a small darker tip, then move on to tapered cylinder tusks.

Still computing tusk geometry and positioning...

Now I'm adding smaller anatomical details: cheek and forehead bumps on the head sphere, a tapering tail built from a curved tube with a tufted end, and tiny toenail details on each foot using small flattened spheres positioned at the front of each foot cylinder.

Working out leg cylinder dimensions and positioning the padded feet, then moving to eyelash placement — computing radial angles around each eye so the lash boxes fan outward naturally and mirror correctly between left and right eyes.

Now I'm detailing the eye structure (sclera, iris, pupil spheres nested at small offsets) and planning the skin texture: a shared canvas-based material with blotches and wrinkle strokes for color plus a separate grayscale bump map, all generated via a seeded random helper for consistent speckling. Setting up the mesh helper and group structure to start writing the actual build code...

Still working through ear geometry and placement...

Working out ear positions so they sit near the head edge without poking too far out, then adding a slight pivot rotation to flare them outward rather than lying flush against the head surface.

I'm setting up the ear geometry with extrusion depth and bevel for the outer grey ear and a thinner flat inner pink shape, then positioning the pivots on either side of the head so the extrusion sits mostly inside the head with the pink inner piece nested just inside the grey ear's outer face.

Working through the geometry: left ear's pink piece should sit at position.x=-0.004 spanning -0.004 to 0, while right ear's mirrors at x=0.012 spanning 0.012 to 0.016, both oriented so the extrusion direction (local z) maps to world x after the pivot rotation.

With that confirmed, I'm checking that the grey ear mesh's 0.8 scale applies in local space before rotation, so the shape and extrusion depth both shrink proportionally — fine. I'll move on to writing the canvas-based skin texture function, generating a procedural texture with some seed-based variation and bump option.

Still writing texture generation... then I'm setting up a Catmull-Rom curve for the trunk, defining a series of control points that curl the tip upward and inward, planning to sample 14 points along it.

For the trunk shape I'm tapering the radius from thick at the base to thin at the tip, using overlapping spheres to create a smooth tube-like form. I'm also roughing out the head, body, and tail with scaled sphere and tube geometries, plus small spheres for a tail tuft and eye components with lashes and a lighter sclera color.

Now I'm positioning the eye on the side of the head, accounting for the head's curvature to figure out how far the eye pokes out at that point, then calculating offsets for the iris and pupil so they sit forward and slightly outward within the sclera without exceeding its surface too much.

Writing eye highlight and lash geometry...

Now I'm starting the actual Three.js implementation, setting up the seeded random generator and beginning to write a texture function that paints a canvas with base skin color and scattered radial gradient patches for mottling.

Writing skin texture code...

Writing ear shape geometry...

Building the ear pivot group...

Checking the pivot tilt direction confirms the ear rotation pushes the top outward correctly for each side, and the scale-before-rotation order in the transform matrix holds up as expected.

Now I'm working through the ear geometry placement — the grey bevel extrusion offsets slightly negative, and the ear shape needs to sit angled back relative to the head's z-center, so I'm adjusting the pivot depth to make sure the ears sit properly against the skull rather than floating off it. Then I'm defining the leg and foot cylinder geometries with their x/z offsets and heights to position the limbs symmetrically under the body.

Toenails are small flattened spheres placed at the foot fronts, spaced across each foot and tinted pale. For the body and head I'm setting up scaled sphere geometries with a forehead bump for added shape, making sure the head sits properly overlapping the body's top. The trunk root anchors at the head's front surface, and the tusks are cylinders rotated to angle forward-down from the mouth area, with the rotation math checked to get the right tip direction.

Positioning the tusks requires nudging them outward and down slightly so they don't collide with the trunk's base radius, recalculating their root position against the head's ellipsoid surface to keep them flush. For the eyelashes, I'm placing small box shapes in an arc around each eye center using angular offsets, mirroring the x-position based on which side the eye is on.

Confirming the rotation math checks out for positioning lashes along the radial arc, and figuring out the lash ring radius should sit just outside the sclera so they droop naturally over the top of the eye.

Now I'm sketching the tail as a tapered tube curve sweeping back and down from the body, with a small tuft cluster of spheres at the tip, and checking that it starts flush with the body's back edge. Then I'm assembling the full material palette -- skin with bump mapping, plus pink, cream, eye white, iris, pupil, lash, and tuft colors -- to keep everything consistent across the mesh.

Building trunk segments as tapered spheres along a curve...

I'm settling on the trunk's radius formula so it tapers smoothly from a thick base to a narrow tip, skipping extra details like nostril bumps or neck wrinkle rings since the texture map should handle that visual richness. Finally I'm confirming the model's grounding -- feet at y=0, overall height around 1.4 units to the ear tips -- so proportions read correctly.

Now I'm structuring the final export function, setting up the texture with a document guard and defining all the materials before writing the complete construction code.
